reason: record_review_from_json.py demands plan-contract verdicts from the protected decomposition twin even after the story shipped (pr_ready cleans only .factory/), taxing every post-ship quickfix quality review; one-line active-decomposition guard + regression test

quality.summary: Minimal correct scoping: verdict enforcement now additionally requires run.json to carry decomposition_status == 'recorded', which the recorder sets at decomposition time and pr_ready strips at ship — so the enforcement window is exactly the active story, unchanged during stories, silent after them. The regression test reproduces the live failure shape (shipped contracts in the protected twin, post-ship run.json, open lite window) and pins acceptance of a verdict-free quality review.

non_blocking_findings.summary: Root cause remains that pr_ready never clears the protected decomposition twin at ship; this guard makes readers scope correctly, but clearing the twin in pr_ready's archive step would remove the stale state class entirely — candidate follow-up, not this window.

performance.summary: One dict lookup added on a CLI path; when the guard is false the recorder now skips a JSON load it previously performed. Net zero-to-negative cost.

security.summary: The lens is whether the guard weakens contract enforcement: it cannot — decomposition_status is 'recorded' for the entire life of an active story (set by the schema-validated recorder, removed only by pr_ready after the contract gate itself has passed), so no review recorded during a story escapes verdict enforcement. Post-ship there is no story to under-review; pr_ready's independent backstop still reads the evidence for the next story.
